investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) — All Remote-Agent Checks Blocked
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". No new agents can be provisioned in the production environment, causing the entire remote-agents feature eval to fail at the creation step before any VM readiness or state assertions can be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 concurrent agents per org (or globally, scope unclear from evidence). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T08:10:46Z), that limit was already at capacity, so POST /api/agents returned 409 with "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three sibling checks depend on successfully creating a new agent via the same endpoint, all fail with the identical error. The eval's expected-output contract (vmIdPresent, remoteState) was never reached — this is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a real quota saturation condition in the production swarm, not a code defect in the agent creation path itself.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} at 2026-06-14T08:10:46.118Z

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is at the shared agent-creation step, not in downstream VM or runtime logic.
Latencies for all three failing checks are low (1395ms, 1202ms, 943ms), consistent with an immediate rejection at the API layer rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.

The expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], but evidence is empty ({}) for all checks — confirming no agent was ever created and no downstream assertions were evaluated.

The error message embeds a nested swarm error: code=conflict, message='conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the quota enforcement originates in the swarm backend, not the AURA API layer itself.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The production swarm org (or global pool) has reached its hard agent quota of 100 and existing agents have not been cleaned up — possibly including stale eval-created agents from prior runs that were not deleted after check completion.
[Likely] The eval harness creates agents but does not reliably delete them after each run (e.g., on failure or timeout), causing quota to accumulate over repeated eval cycles.
[Possible] A separate workload or user activity in the same production org/swarm namespace consumed quota independently of the eval harness, leaving no headroom for eval agent creation.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or was recently lowered in the swarm backend, reducing available capacity below what the eval harness expects.
[Less likely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents toward the quota (e.g., counting terminated or errored agents as still active).

reproductionSteps.details: Check whether 100 agents are currently registered and in what states (running, idle, error, terminated).

reproductionSteps.details: This confirms the quota saturation is still active and not a transient condition at eval run time.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect swarm quota configuration
reproductionSteps.details: Review swarm backend configuration to confirm the limit=100 value, its scope (per-org vs. global), and whether it was recently changed.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the eval after freeing quota
reproductionSteps.details: Delete or terminate stale agents to bring the count below 100, then re-trigger the remote-agent-create eval check to confirm it passes when quota is available.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Agent Creation Checks
investigation.summary: All three Remote Agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T08:10:47–49Z with identical HTTP 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to exercise the lifecycle, so no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected.
investigation.rootCause: The eval harness issues POST /api/agents to create a disposable agent before polling its state and runtime. The swarm backend rejected every creation attempt with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the target org or global swarm namespace has already reached its maximum of 100 concurrent agents. Because creation is a prerequisite for all downstream checks, all three sibling checks failed with the same error before any lifecycle state could be observed. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence of user-traffic impact is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1395 ms, ended 08:10:47.513Z), remote-agent-state (latency 1202 ms, ended 08:10:48.715Z), remote-agent-runtime (latency 943 ms, ended 08:10:49.658Z).

Error body is identical across all three checks: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the namespace has hit its hard cap.

All three checks have empty evidence objects, confirming no required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were populated — consistent with failure at the creation step before any state could be read.
Latency for all three calls is well under the warning threshold (5000 ms) and outage threshold (20000 ms), indicating the 409 is a fast rejection, not a timeout or infrastructure outage.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Leaked or orphaned eval agents from previous eval runs were never cleaned up, accumulating until the 100-agent quota was exhausted. The eval harness may lack a reliable teardown/cleanup step.
[Likely] The eval environment shares an agent quota with other workloads (e.g., other eval suites, staging traffic, or developer testing), and concurrent usage pushed the count to the limit.
[Possible] A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup phase, leaving one or more agents stranded and permanently consuming quota slots.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is too low for the volume of concurrent eval runs scheduled in this environment, causing a race condition under normal eval cadence.

[Unlikely] The 409 'swarm agent already exists' phrasing could indicate the eval is reusing a deterministic agent ID that already exists, rather than a global quota issue — however, the inner error explicitly says 'quota exceeded', making ID collision the less likely interpretation.

reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents?limit=100 (inspect total count in response against the 100-agent limit)

reproductionSteps.command: GET /api/agents (filter results for agents matching eval harness naming conventions or with stale creation timestamps)

reproductionSteps.command: POST /api/agents (with minimal valid payload; expect HTTP 409 if quota is still exhausted)

reproductionSteps.label: Delete confirmed orphaned or stale eval agents to free quota slots
reproductionSteps.command: DELETE /api/agents/{agentId} (for each identified orphaned agent)

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the failing eval suite after cleanup to confirm all three checks pass
reproductionSteps.details: Trigger remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks and verify HTTP 201 on creation and populated evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state).

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T08:10:47–49Z with identical HTTP 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle assertions, so no expected-output contract evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the "hello from aura" assertion was never reached.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is returning "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call. The eval harness attempts to create a fresh agent at the start of each check run; because the quota is exhausted, agent creation fails with 409 before any lifecycle step can proceed. This is a resource-exhaustion condition in the swarm layer, not a latency or connectivity failure — all three checks failed at the first creation step with identical error payloads, and latency (943–1395 ms) is well within the warning threshold (20 000 ms), confirming the service responded promptly but rejected the request on quota grounds.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with the identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the hard cap of 100 swarm agents has been reached in the target environment.

Failure timestamps are sequential (remote-agent-create ended 08:10:47.513Z, remote-agent-state ended 08:10:48.715Z, remote-agent-runtime ended 08:10:49.658Z), consistent with a single eval run where each check independently attempted POST /api/agents and was rejected at the same quota wall.
Latency for all three checks (1395 ms, 1202 ms, 943 ms) is far below the warning threshold of 20 000 ms, ruling out timeout or network degradation as a contributing factor.

No expected-output contract evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were populated (evidence: {}), confirming the failure occurred at agent creation before any downstream runtime interaction.

The outer error message 'swarm agent already exists' alongside the inner 'quota exceeded' suggests the swarm may also be detecting a pre-existing leaked or un-cleaned eval agent occupying a quota slot, compounding the exhaustion.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Swarm agent quota (limit: 100) is fully consumed by live or leaked agents — possibly including agents from previous eval runs that were not torn down — leaving no capacity for the eval harness to create a new agent.
[Likely contributing] The eval harness does not perform a pre-run cleanup or reuse an existing eval agent; it always issues a fresh POST /api/agents, which fails immediately when quota is exhausted.
[Possible] Previous eval runs or manual provisioning left zombie/orphaned agents in the swarm that count against the quota but are not actively used, gradually filling the 100-slot limit.
[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is a hard per-environment or per-org cap that has not been raised to accommodate the current number of active agents plus eval overhead.
[Less likely] A misconfiguration in the eval check causes it to create agents without a corresponding delete/teardown step, causing quota to grow monotonically over repeated eval runs.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED: Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable (404)
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately (2001 ms) because the agent runtime returned a 404 on session open, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields — frameTypes (containing generation_completed) and imageUrlPresent — are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past the error state.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response on session open indicates either the harness process is not running, the route path has changed in a recent deployment (version mismatch), or the environment variable pointing to the harness URL is misconfigured or stale in the production environment. This is an eval-environment / infrastructure failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].event = 'generation_error' with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, confirming the stream terminated at session-open before any progress frames were emitted.
Error message explicitly states 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404)' and instructs to verify LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.
failedCheck.message confirms both required evidence fields 'frameTypes' and 'imageUrlPresent' are missing — no generation_completed frame was ever received.
Stream sequence is: generation_start → generation_error → empty message frame. The expected sequence (progress frames → generation_completed → artifact URL) was never reached.
latencyMs = 2001 ms with endedAt - startedAt ≈ 2 s, consistent with a fast network-level rejection (404) rather than a timeout or slow model failure.
failedCheck.status = 'fail' in environment = 'production' (eval environment), with no sibling checks or user-traffic signals supplied.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Harness process is not running or crashed in the eval environment — the 404 is returned by an upstream router or load balancer because no backend is registered at the expected path.
[Likely] Version mismatch after a recent deployment: the harness was updated and the session-open route path changed, making the previously configured URL return 404.
[Likely] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured, empty, or points to a stale/decommissioned host in the production eval environment.

[Possible] Network policy, firewall rule, or service-mesh routing change is blocking or mis-routing requests to the harness endpoint, causing the router to return 404 instead of forwarding the request.
[Less likely] The eval harness deployment was rolled back or never promoted to the production environment, leaving the old (now absent) endpoint registered.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED: Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable (404)
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately (2001 ms) because the agent runtime returned a 404 on session open, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields — frameTypes (containing generation_completed) and imageUrlPresent — are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past the error state.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response on session open indicates either the harness process is not running, the route path has changed in a recent deployment (version mismatch), or the environment variable pointing to the harness URL is misconfigured or stale in the production environment. This is an eval-environment / infrastructure failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].event = 'generation_error' with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, confirming the stream terminated at session-open before any progress frames were emitted.
Error message explicitly states 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404)' and instructs to verify LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.
failedCheck.message confirms both required evidence fields 'frameTypes' and 'imageUrlPresent' are missing — no generation_completed frame was ever received.
Stream sequence is: generation_start → generation_error → empty message frame. The expected sequence (progress frames → generation_completed → artifact URL) was never reached.
latencyMs = 2001 ms with endedAt - startedAt ≈ 2 s, consistent with a fast network-level rejection (404) rather than a timeout or slow model failure.
failedCheck.status = 'fail' in environment = 'production' (eval environment), with no sibling checks or user-traffic signals supplied.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Harness process is not running or crashed in the eval environment — the 404 is returned by an upstream router or load balancer because no backend is registered at the expected path.
[Likely] Version mismatch after a recent deployment: the harness was updated and the session-open route path changed, making the previously configured URL return 404.
[Likely] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured, empty, or points to a stale/decommissioned host in the production eval environment.

[Possible] Network policy, firewall rule, or service-mesh routing change is blocking or mis-routing requests to the harness endpoint, causing the router to return 404 instead of forwarding the request.
[Less likely] The eval harness deployment was rolled back or never promoted to the production environment, leaving the old (now absent) endpoint registered.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) — All Remote-Agent Checks Blocked
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". No new agents can be provisioned in the production environment, causing the entire remote-agents feature eval to fail at the creation step before any VM readiness or state assertions can be evaluated.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 concurrent agents per org (or globally, scope unclear from evidence). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T08:10:46Z), that limit was already at capacity, so POST /api/agents returned 409 with "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three sibling checks depend on successfully creating a new agent via the same endpoint, all fail with the identical error. The eval's expected-output contract (vmIdPresent, remoteState) was never reached — this is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a real quota saturation condition in the production swarm, not a code defect in the agent creation path itself.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} at 2026-06-14T08:10:46.118Z

All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) carry the identical 409 error message, confirming the failure is at the shared agent-creation step, not in downstream VM or runtime logic.
Latencies for all three failing checks are low (1395ms, 1202ms, 943ms), consistent with an immediate rejection at the API layer rather than a timeout or infrastructure hang.

The expected-output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], but evidence is empty ({}) for all checks — confirming no agent was ever created and no downstream assertions were evaluated.

The error message embeds a nested swarm error: code=conflict, message='conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', indicating the quota enforcement originates in the swarm backend, not the AURA API layer itself.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The production swarm org (or global pool) has reached its hard agent quota of 100 and existing agents have not been cleaned up — possibly including stale eval-created agents from prior runs that were not deleted after check completion.
[Likely] The eval harness creates agents but does not reliably delete them after each run (e.g., on failure or timeout), causing quota to accumulate over repeated eval cycles.
[Possible] A separate workload or user activity in the same production org/swarm namespace consumed quota independently of the eval harness, leaving no headroom for eval agent creation.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or was recently lowered in the swarm backend, reducing available capacity below what the eval harness expects.
[Less likely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents toward the quota (e.g., counting terminated or errored agents as still active).

The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to exercise the lifecycle, so no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected.
investigations.rootCause: The eval harness issues POST /api/agents to create a disposable agent before polling its state and runtime. The swarm backend rejected every creation attempt with HTTP 409 and the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the target org or global swarm namespace has already reached its maximum of 100 concurrent agents. Because creation is a prerequisite for all downstream checks, all three sibling checks failed with the same error before any lifecycle state could be observed. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence of user-traffic impact is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1395 ms, ended 08:10:47.513Z), remote-agent-state (latency 1202 ms, ended 08:10:48.715Z), remote-agent-runtime (latency 943 ms, ended 08:10:49.658Z).

Error body is identical across all three checks: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the namespace has hit its hard cap.

All three checks have empty evidence objects, confirming no required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were populated — consistent with failure at the creation step before any state could be read.
Latency for all three calls is well under the warning threshold (5000 ms) and outage threshold (20000 ms), indicating the 409 is a fast rejection, not a timeout or infrastructure outage.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Leaked or orphaned eval agents from previous eval runs were never cleaned up, accumulating until the 100-agent quota was exhausted. The eval harness may lack a reliable teardown/cleanup step.
[Likely] The eval environment shares an agent quota with other workloads (e.g., other eval suites, staging traffic, or developer testing), and concurrent usage pushed the count to the limit.
[Possible] A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup phase, leaving one or more agents stranded and permanently consuming quota slots.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 is too low for the volume of concurrent eval runs scheduled in this environment, causing a race condition under normal eval cadence.

[Unlikely] The 409 'swarm agent already exists' phrasing could indicate the eval is reusing a deterministic agent ID that already exists, rather than a global quota issue — however, the inner error explicitly says 'quota exceeded', making ID collision the less likely interpretation.
